record.question: What should the patient be told to expect during the intravenous contrast injection?
options: A warm, flushed sensation and a metallic taste in their mouth.
A feeling of coldness spreading through their body.
Pain and numbness at the injection site.
Shortness of breath and difficulty breathing.
record.explanation: Answer A: A warm, flushed sensation and a metallic taste in their mouth.. A transient warm/flushed sensation and metallic taste can occur with IV iodinated contrast injection. Reference: https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/bodyct; https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Contrast-Manual. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
